name: Water Bakunawa
iocPatterns: Targeting of industrial control systems in water/wastewater
keyCapabilities: Sophisticated evasion of security monitoring systems
recommendedActions: Patch known vulnerabilities such as Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) immediately.
Deploy security solutions capable of detecting and alerting on EDR-disabling behaviors.
Implement strictly segmented networks for critical infrastructure components like water distribution systems.
Develop robust, offline backup strategies to mitigate RansomHub encryption impact.
Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across all administrative and remote access points.
Monitor system logs for unauthorized modifications of service executables or security agents.
Enhance visibility into lateral movement within the network using internal traffic analysis.
Conduct routine audits of EDR/antivirus integrity to ensure they have not been tamed by automated tools.
campaignsText: Water Bakunawa operates with a high level of sophistication, often operating within the RaaS landscape alongside groups like ALPHV. Their campaign patterns show a move toward targeting critical infrastructure to maximize pressure. They demonstrate high operational discipline by utilizing tools specifically engineered to evade modern security tech (EDRKillShifter) for as long as possible during an intrusion.
description: Water Bakunawa is a sophisticated cybercriminal group specializing in RansomHub ransomware and advanced anti-EDR techniques to bypass security monitoring. They specifically target high-value sectors including critical infrastructure (water/wastewater), healthcare, and finance.
goals: The primary strategic goal of Water Bakunawa is financially motivated extortion through the deployment of ransomware. They target critical infrastructure (water/wastewater), healthcare, and financial services because these sectors are highly sensitive to downtime and data loss, providing maximum leverage for making ransom demands. Their involvement in the RaaS ecosystem suggests they may hunt for victims who have a higher willingness or necessity to pay quickly to restore operations.
